terminal_name: Bajo Alto natural gas liquefaction plant (Petroecuador)
issue: Discovery sweep surfaced EP Petroecuador's Bajo Alto liquefaction plant (El Guabo canton, El Oro province), operating since 2011, processing ~100 t/day (design 200 t/day) of gas from the offshore Amistad field for domestic LNG trucking/distribution. It is NOT in GEM. Assessed as out of scope: a small-scale onshore satellite/peak-shaving liquefaction plant feeding domestic ground distribution, not a marine LNG import/export terminal. Flagging only so a reviewer can confirm the scope judgment. Geographically adjacent to the GEM Jambeli FSRU (also Bajo Alto) but a distinct facility.
suggested_action: Confirm out-of-scope (domestic small-scale liquefaction, not a marine import/export terminal); no GEM action expected. If methodology scope ever extends to domestic satellite plants, revisit.

issue: On 26 June 2025 LipiAndes announced acquisition of 70% of Sycar (the Jambeli FSRU sponsor), entering Ecuador to expand LNG supply. GEM already reflects this (Parent: 'LipiAndes [70.0%]; Sycar LLC [30.0%]'), so ownership is current. Note also: as of reporting through 2025 the full FSRU remains a proposal contingent on a combined-cycle power project (targeted 2026-27); current activity is land-based LNG trucking from Peru (first land import Nov 2024) and ISO-tank deliveries, not yet a moored FSRU. Status appears correctly 'proposed' in GEM. fetch_timeline is DOWN so no timeline edit staged.
suggested_action: No change needed; verify 'proposed' status holds and ownership/parent shares remain LipiAndes 70% / Sycar 30% at next Update. Watch for FSRU FID tied to the combined-cycle power tender.
